newsitem.title: GERMANY: Adidas profit growth slowed but U.S. sales gain.
newsitem.headline: Adidas profit growth slowed but U.S. sales gain.

text.p: German sportswear group Adidas AG said Wednesday its double-digit profit growth slowed in the second quarter due to the impact of higher tax rates, although its U.S. performance improved.

Adidas said net income rose 20 percent to 69 million marks ($36.7 million) behind a 37 percent rise in sales to 1.427 billion marks ($760 million), particularly in North America, where it has begun reaping the benefits of an aggressive advertising campaign.
But the group said its income tax payments surged 112 percent over the 1996 second quarter to 34 million marks ($18 million), which put a drag on earnings growth.
For the first half of the year, Adidas said net income rose 29 percent to 238 million marks ($127 million), while sales were up 40 percent to 3.14 billion marks ($1.67 billion).
Adidas said apparel remained the major growth driver in the first six months of 1997. Footwear, helped the most by running shoes, rose 29 percent and outperformed the market.
Sales in North America, where Adidas has sought to take on global leaders Nike and Reebok on their home turf, grew 51 percent during the first half of the year to 727 million marks ($387 million).

Adidas has signed a number of major sponsorship deals in the United States, including a deal with the New York Yankees baseball team, to boost its market share to 10 to 15 percent by the year 2000 from its 1996 level of about 5 percent.

Other notable high-profile sponsorship deals in the United States include professional basketball star Kobe Bryant of the Los Angeles Lakers and college sports teams at Northwestern University and the University of Notre Dame.
